title: Singly linked lists
syllabusDesc: Link nodes together so inserts/removals in the middle stay O(1).
desc: A linked list stores each element in a node that points to the next node. It trades fast middle inserts/removals for slower indexing (O(n)).
solution:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

# Build list: 1 -> 2 -> 4
head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(4)))

# Insert 3 after 2
current = head
while current:
    if current.value == 2:
        current.next = Node(3, current.next)
        break
    current = current.next

# Traverse
current = head
values = []
while current:
    values.append(current.value)
    current = current.next
print(values)
techniques: Traverse with a while loop and a cursor pointer
Track head/tail when adding or removing nodes
challenges: Delete a node with a given value (handle head separately)
Find the middle of a list with slow/fast pointers
notes:
Indexing is O(n); use only when frequent middle inserts/removals justify it.

Be careful to keep references when rewiring next pointers.
